# TC-RECYCLING-01 — preserved-history reconciliation

**Controlling review:** TEX-EXACT-2026-10-11, TEX-01. **Scope:** the enemy-cause predicate for Efficient Recycling only. This is the expressly requested consequential reconciliation, not a new class-card or recipe promotion.

Keep the actual `tinker.hero.techsmith.efficient-recycling` card and the reviewed `DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST.md` Destruction row: **enemy cause is not required**. Your qualifying destroyed non-copy device, no deliberate sacrifice, reachable usable unspent debris, one minute after combat, the once-per-short-rest allowance, actual deployment RP, inherited source exclusions and exclusive material consumption remain required. A qualifying refund is at most min(1 RP, RP actually paid to deploy that same instance). The first successful material consumer spends that instance's usable debris; Snap or a second destruction does not create another material opportunity. Administrative ending is not destruction.

The later instruction “KEEP actual enemy destruction” in TD-13 of the final advanced source verdict `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ADVANCED_167_SOURCE_AUTHORING_VERDICT.md` (SHA-256 `48f885becd03e4a99ba8d6243ce286c1e1e88cfefc776af9ff89a9182c79c8e0`), and the derived current crafting-guide phrase “after its genuine enemy destruction”, are superseded **only as restrictions on Efficient Recycling**. That later narrowing is not retained. The remainder of TD-13's deployment-cost distinction and its other restrictions remain. Use the full corrected public/internal paragraphs in `TEX_01_04_CORRECTIONS.json`.

Preserve the original advanced source verdict, its 13-file package, submitted revisions, conflict/proposal record, original class card, lifecycle guide, reference helper, existing regression and prior promotion receipts exactly as historical evidence. Do not rewrite an old “unapplied” preparation to imply the correction was already in force. Attach this erratum and a new version-bound application receipt to the current derived guide/envelope changes. Retain original `sourceVerdictSha256` values as historical provenance and add the explicit controlling reconciliation; do not attribute corrected wording to unchanged source bytes.

The affected current texts are the public advanced operating guide and `/operatingGuideText`; the internal advanced guide's TD-13 and `/procedureSections/TD-13/text`; and the Tinker pending-conflict sentence in `CLASS_RESOURCE_REFERENCE.md`. Refresh current artifact hashes and the five current TC-RECYCLING-01 coverage notes without closing their broader areas. None of the 167 recipe-card objects, 100 public recipe-card objects, 48 class-interface source cards, body models, host templates or their original sources changes.

For ordinary crafted Tinkering deployments, recipe-585–623 and recipe-684–687 supply no innate RP deployment cost. Their GP price, later activation RP, Field Repair RP and service inputs do not create refundable deployment RP. A different explicitly authorized paid deployment still requires its actual instance/payment history; this erratum creates no such permission.

Scrap Salvage keeps its enemy-destroyed-material predicate. Scrap Reaper keeps its enemy-hit predicate, actual Reaction/cost/range/frequency and no-deployable-slot lifecycle override. Volatile Components keeps its own enemy-cause and exclusion rules. Distinguish a copied device from copied incoming damage and retain the actual inherited branch flags. The Recycling reconciliation does not authorize those other effects from friendly or accidental causes.

Fulfilled LAX, NWX, LRX and 687/433 recipe scopes remain fulfilled. This erratum establishes no broader class, feat, spell, runtime, human balance/teaching or whole-game approval. corrections.decision: Restore automatic Crimson Agent 9 Blood Gauge capacity; do not grant BG.

operations.old: **Blood Gauge maximum: 3; 6 with Spill Control.** Begin and end encounters at 0. Once on your regular turn, a weapon attack damaging a hostile living creature grants 1 BG; Hemorrhage Slash shares that trigger. All gains, including explicit refunds or critical/kill gains, total at most 2 per round. Staged, friendly and sacrificial sources do not qualify.
operations.replacement: **Blood Gauge maximum: 3, becoming 6 automatically at Crimson Agent 9; a known Spill Control grants capacity 6 earlier, never more than 6.** Increasing capacity does not grant Blood Gauge. Begin and end encounters at 0. Once on your regular turn, a weapon attack damaging a hostile living creature grants 1 BG; Hemorrhage Slash shares that trigger. All gains, including explicit refunds or critical/kill gains, total at most 2 per round. Staged, friendly and sacrificial sources do not qualify.

corrections.decision: Replace unspecified turn-boundary recharge timing with actual regular-turn-start timing and exact source endpoints.

operations.section: End a turn, end an encounter, finish a rest: first paragraph
operations.old: At a regular turn boundary, resolve actual deadlines and tick round-recharge counters under the [timing rules](../mechanics/CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md#action-and-timing-limits). An extra Action or extra turn does not supply another regular-turn recharge tick. A named counter can receive at most one reset/shortening per round, and a reset is neither a resource refill nor an extra activation.
operations.replacement: Resolve each deadline at its actual source-defined start, end or elapsed-time endpoint. Tick round-recharge counters once at the start of the owner's regular turn, even when the owner cannot act, under the [timing rules](../mechanics/CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md#action-and-timing-limits). A turn end, extra Action or extra turn does not supply another regular-turn recharge tick. Outside initiative, use the same source's six-second elapsed-time procedure without double counting a boundary. Only a positive counter can be reset or shortened, at most once per named ability per numbered round; a reset is neither a resource refill nor an extra activation.

corrections.decision: State that Core task degrees are the default, not an override of six-band crafting or no-natural-shift dismantling.

The Core default uses four outcome degrees and natural-1/20 shifts; when it supplies only success/failure effects, apply those shifts and then collapse the degrees.
